evidence: Receiving DO2 online sensor: ~10.02 mg/L at 48.0 h → 2.99 at 48.2 h → 1.80 mg/L at 52.0 h, crossing the 2.0 mg/L minimum
Delayed assay: P = 0.98 g/L (36h), 2.82 g/L (48h); source batches reached ~8 g/L by 72h — growth ongoing, high OUR

Forward model (source-calibrated, nominal): transfer multiplier 0.438; strong_feed_reduction min DO 1.16 mg/L, deficit 3.88 mg·h/L, 172.6 kg product — best among keep/reduce_feed/increase_air/combined
All four non-stop actions infeasible per nominal model; strong_feed_reduction has smallest oxygen-deficit integral and retains product mass
args.rationale: Receiving DO2 collapsed below the 2.0 mg/L minimum at ~48.2 h and sits at ~1.8 mg/L at the 52 h decision time, driven by impaired oxygen transfer (model-estimated transfer multiplier ~0.44). Aeration-only and mild feed cuts cannot close the deficit (model min DO 0.87–0.99, below-limit 9–11 h). A strong feed reduction to 0.6× cuts oxygen uptake enough to minimize the oxygen-constraint violation (min DO ~1.16, deficit integral ~3.9 vs 8.3 for aeration-only) while actually retaining the highest predicted product mass (~172.6 kg vs ~171.3–171.5 kg for milder actions, due to less dilution) and keeping the batch running to 96 h instead of stopping (zero counted production). This is the best bounded intervention available given the constraint cannot be fully satisfied.
args.uncertainty: The forward model is source-calibrated and imperfect: all five sensitivity members remain infeasible, so the true receiving process may differ (better or worse). The DO2 deficit magnitude and the 0.44 transfer multiplier are estimates; if receiving transfer capacity is better than modeled, strong feed reduction is a conservative, product-preserving choice; if worse, no bounded action avoids constraint violation and a stop/abort decision would need escalation. Assay delay (4 h) means action must be taken on online sensor data.
